about: Daily Scoop posts for laporteweathernow.com, newest first. Publish and correct posts with laporteweathernow.com/scoop-draft. Never change a forecast after it is posted; add a dated correction instead.

posts.title: Sunny and dry all week; coldest morning Tuesday, near 41
posts.summary: Sunny and dry through the week in the NWS forecast, with a chilly start Tuesday near 41, highs warming from the mid 60s to the low and mid 70s by the weekend, and no watches, warnings or advisories for La Porte County.
body: Today (Monday): sunny, with a high near 66 and a north wind around 5 mph. Tonight: clear and cold, with a low around 41 and a calm to light east wind. No rain is in the forecast, and NWS hour-by-hour rain chances show today dry through work hours (6 a.m. to 6 p.m.). At 5:15 a.m. the La Porte airport reported clear skies and 45 degrees, with the dew point also at 45 (100% humidity) and a light northwest wind at 3 mph. NWS Northern Indiana says patches of light fog or mist are possible on these cool mornings, so allow a little extra time if you hit a foggy stretch, and if you have tender plants or animals outside, tonight is the night to cover or bring them in.

Tuesday: sunny, with a high near 70 and a south wind 5 to 10 mph; Tuesday night mostly clear, with a low around 54. Wednesday: sunny, with a high near 72 (low around 52). Thursday: sunny, with a high near 68 (low around 48). Friday: mostly sunny, with a high near 68 (low around 47). Saturday: sunny, with a high near 72 (low around 53). Sunday: mostly sunny and warmer, with a high near 76 (low around 55 Sunday night). The NWS forecast has no rain at all through Sunday night. The four computer models we also check agree with NWS within a few degrees for Tuesday and Wednesday.

What changed since yesterday's Scoop: very little, and the week stays dry. Tonight's low is around 41 (from 40), Tuesday's high is near 70 (from 68), Tuesday night's low is around 54 (from 52), Thursday night's low is around 48 (from 47), Friday's high is near 68 (from 69), and Saturday night's low is around 53 (from 51). Today's high is near 66 (from 65). Sunday is now in the forecast, mostly sunny with a high near 76. This morning NWS Northern Indiana forecasters call it a pretty uneventful week, with cool, brisk mornings the biggest story. Tonight into Tuesday morning is the coldest, with lows in the low 40s to upper 30s, especially north of US 6, which includes La Porte. They say a few patches of light frost are possible, mostly on car roofs and rooftops, but dew points look high enough that most surfaces will just get dew; they still suggest protecting temperature-sensitive plants and animals to be safe. Highs start a bit below normal and end the week a bit above, in the low to mid 70s (normal is 67 at South Bend), and the next chance of rain looks to come late in the weekend.

Right now there are no watches, warnings or advisories for La Porte County, northern or southern, and none for Porter or Lake counties next door. On Lake Michigan, NWS Northern Indiana has a Small Craft Advisory until 10 a.m. for the waters from Michigan City up to St. Joseph, Mich. The Weather Prediction Center has no flooding-rain risk for La Porte for the next five days. The Storm Prediction Center has no thunderstorm or severe risk at La Porte today through Wednesday, and no severe risk areas anywhere in the country.

posts.title: Dry, sunny week ahead; a chilly Tuesday morning near 40
posts.summary: Sunny and dry through the week in the NWS forecast, with highs from the mid 60s to low 70s, a low around 40 Tuesday morning, and no watches, warnings or advisories for La Porte County.
body: Automatic update, 10:02 p.m.: It's running cooler than NWS's earlier hour-by-hour forecast: at 9:35 p.m. the La Porte airport reported light rain and fog/mist and 48 degrees, where that forecast had about 54. NWS's earlier hour-by-hour forecast gave that hour no chance of rain. There are no watches, warnings, or advisories for La Porte County right now.

This afternoon (Sunday): sunny, with a high near 68 and a northwest wind around 10 mph behind this afternoon's dry cold front. At 3:55 p.m. the La Porte airport reported clear skies and 70 degrees, a little warmer than the forecast high, with a north-northwest wind at 13 mph. Tonight: clear, with a low around 48 and a northwest wind 5 to 10 mph. No rain is in the forecast, and NWS hour-by-hour rain chances show Monday dry through work hours (6 a.m. to 6 p.m.). If you have tender plants outside, Monday night is the one to watch.

Monday: sunny and cooler, with a high near 65 and a light north wind. Monday night: clear, with a low around 40 and a calm to light east wind. NWS Northern Indiana says patchy frost is possible Tuesday morning, mostly in outlying areas north of the Toll Road, though some high clouds may keep it from getting cold enough. Then it warms: sunny Tuesday with a high near 68 (low around 52 Tuesday night), sunny Wednesday with a high near 72 (low around 51), mostly sunny Thursday with a high near 68 (low around 47), mostly sunny Friday with a high near 69 (low around 45), and sunny Saturday with a high near 72 (low around 51 Saturday night). The NWS forecast has no rain at all through Saturday night. The four computer models we also check agree with NWS within a couple of degrees for Monday and Tuesday.

What changed since Thursday's Scoop (the newest one we wrote; Friday through this morning were automatic NWS updates): the start of the week is milder. Monday's high is now near 65 (from 61), Monday night's low is around 40 (from 38), and Tuesday's high is near 68 (from 63). Today's high is 68 (from 67) and tonight's low is 48 (from 45). Wednesday's slight chance of a shower (from 15%) is gone; the forecast is dry all week. This afternoon NWS Northern Indiana forecasters say a reinforcing shot of cool air follows this morning's cold front, with highs in the 60s Monday and slightly above normal by late week, upper 60s to upper 70s across their area. They expect dry weather to continue; a front stalls nearby midweek without rain, and the next chance of rain could come as early as Saturday night but may wait until Sunday or Sunday night, as a slow-moving storm system brings moisture up from the south. Yesterday (Saturday) we said a high of 65 and a low of 42; the La Porte airport got 70 and 46.

Right now there are no watches, warnings or advisories for La Porte County, northern or southern, and none for Porter or Lake counties next door; NWS Northern Indiana lists none anywhere in its area. The Weather Prediction Center has no flooding-rain risk for La Porte for the next five days. The Storm Prediction Center has no thunderstorm or severe risk at La Porte today through Tuesday; today's only severe risk area is a Marginal Risk far away, over the Florida Panhandle and far southern Alabama.

The next few days, from the same NWS forecast: Sunday Night: Mostly clear, low around 46. Monday: Sunny, high near 63. Monday Night: Clear, low around 39. Tuesday: Sunny, high near 67. Tuesday Night: Mostly clear, low around 47. Wednesday: Sunny, high near 70.

posts.title: Showers and a few storms this afternoon and tonight, then a dry, cool weekend
posts.summary: Showers are likely today (70%), with showers and thunderstorms tonight (90%) adding up to about seven tenths of an inch to 1¼ inches in the NWS forecast by early Friday; the Weather Prediction Center has La Porte in a Slight Risk for flooding rain through Friday morning, and the weekend is sunny and cooler.
body: Update, 2:43 p.m.: Still dry so far, and warmer than forecast: 79 and clear at the La Porte airport at 2:15. The rain is still on the way. The Weather Service expects about an inch, give or take, by Friday morning from rich Gulf moisture, with the heaviest downpours tonight. Flood Watches are already up to our west in Lake County and around Chicago. Out west, a record-strength El Niño is fueling the Pacific hurricanes behind this week's flooding in New Mexico and Texas; the latest El Niño numbers are on our World Disaster Watch page.

Today (Thursday): rain showers likely before 4 p.m., then showers and thunderstorms likely, cloudy, with a high near 77 and a southwest wind 5 to 10 mph. The chance of rain is 70%, and NWS says a tenth to a quarter of an inch is possible. Tonight brings the main rain: showers and thunderstorms (90%), a low around 55 as the wind turns north at 5 to 10 mph, and a half to three quarters of an inch possible. At 5:15 a.m. the La Porte airport reported cloudy skies and 64 degrees, with the dew point also at 64 and a nearly calm wind. If you're out tonight, expect heavy downpours in spots; slow down on wet roads and never drive into water covering the road.

Friday: a chance of showers before 6 a.m. (30%, with another tenth to a quarter of an inch possible), then mostly sunny and cooler, with a high near 63 and a north wind around 10 mph. Added up, the NWS forecast for La Porte comes to about seven tenths of an inch to 1¼ inches from today through early Friday. Then it stays dry for days: clear Friday night with a low around 42, sunny Saturday with a high near 65 (low around 43 Saturday night), sunny Sunday with a high near 67 (low around 45), and sunny Monday with a high near 61. Monday night is the chilly one, clear with a low around 38, then sunny Tuesday with a high near 63. The next slight chance of a shower (15%) is Wednesday afternoon.

What changed since yesterday's Scoop: the rain looks lighter and ends sooner. Today's chance is 70% (from 80%), with a tenth to a quarter of an inch (from a quarter to a half), and the high rose to 77 (from 73). Tonight stays at 90%, with a low of 55 (from 56) and a half to three quarters of an inch (from three quarters of an inch to an inch). Friday's showers now end before 6 a.m. instead of lasting into the early afternoon, the chance fell to 30% (from 70%), and the high is 63 (from 64). The NWS total through Friday fell to about seven tenths of an inch to 1¼ inches (from 1¼ to 2 inches for the same stretch). The weekend changed little: Sunday's high is 67 (from 65), and Monday night's low is 38 (from 37). This morning NWS Northern Indiana forecasters say a cold front will push the rain that has sat just to our north and west south through the area today and tonight; any storms should stay weak, but heavy downpours are possible, and overall flood concerns appear low. They expect dry weather with highs in the 60s this weekend into next week, with Tuesday morning the coldest, in the upper 30s, and suggest getting furnaces tuned up for the season. Yesterday we said a high of 73; the La Porte airport got 64.

Right now there are no watches, warnings, or advisories for La Porte County, northern or southern, and none for Porter or Lake counties next door. The Weather Prediction Center (part of the National Weather Service) has La Porte County in a Slight Risk of flooding rain from 7 a.m. today to 7 a.m. Friday (at least a 15% chance); NWS Northern Indiana notes that most of its area is in the lower Marginal Risk, with the Slight Risk mainly in its western counties, which include ours. There's no flooding-rain risk for La Porte after Friday morning. The Storm Prediction Center has La Porte in its general thunderstorm area today, meaning storms are possible but not expected to be severe, and it expects no severe storms anywhere in the U.S. today through Saturday.

posts.title: Rainy through midday Friday, heaviest Thursday night, with flooding possible in low spots
posts.summary: Showers today (90%) and tonight (70%), then showers and thunderstorms Thursday and Thursday night (80% and 90%), adding up to about 1½ to 2½ inches in the NWS forecast by Friday afternoon; the Weather Prediction Center has La Porte in a Slight Risk for flooding rain Thursday into Friday morning, and the weekend turns dry and cooler.
body: Today (Wednesday): rain showers and mostly cloudy, with a high near 68 and a south wind 5 to 10 mph. The chance of rain is 90%, and NWS says a tenth to a quarter of an inch is possible; forecasters expect the best chance of showers near Lake Michigan in the middle and late afternoon. At 6:55 a.m. the La Porte airport reported cloudy skies and 59 degrees, with the dew point also at 59 and a nearly calm wind. Tonight: showers likely (70%), cloudy, with a low around 62 and a south wind 5 to 10 mph, and another tenth to a quarter of an inch possible.

Thursday: showers likely before 5 p.m., then showers and thunderstorms, with a high near 73, a south wind around 5 mph, and an 80% chance of rain; a quarter to a half inch is possible. Thursday night brings the heaviest rain: showers and thunderstorms (90%), a low around 56, a west wind around 5 mph, and three quarters of an inch to an inch possible. Friday: showers likely before 2 p.m. (70%, with another quarter to half inch possible), then partly sunny, with a high near 64 and a north wind 5 to 10 mph. Added up, the NWS forecast for La Porte comes to about 1½ to 2½ inches from today through Friday afternoon. Then it dries out and cools down: mostly clear Friday night with a low around 43, sunny Saturday with a high near 65, mostly sunny Sunday (high near 65), and sunny Monday with a high near 60, with a chilly low around 37 Monday night.

What changed since yesterday's Scoop: the rain arrives sooner and heavier. Today's chance jumped to 90% (from 30%) and its high fell to 68 (from 73). Tonight rose to 70% (from 20%), with a low of 62 (from 63). Thursday rose to 80% (from 60%) and now includes thunderstorms later in the day, and its high fell to 73 (from 76). Thursday night rose to 90% (from 80%), with a low of 56 (from 57), and Friday rose to 70% (from 50%). NWS rain amounts went up as well: a quarter to a half inch Thursday (from a tenth to a quarter) and three quarters of an inch to an inch Thursday night (from a half to three quarters). Yesterday, NWS Northern Indiana forecasters expected around an inch for most locations and no significant flooding. This morning they point to the Weather Prediction Center's Marginal Risk for excessive rainfall later today and Slight Risk for Thursday, and they still don't expect severe weather. The dry, cooler weekend is still on track.

Right now there are no watches, warnings, or advisories for La Porte County. Next door, NWS Chicago issued a Hydrologic Outlook at 3:59 a.m. for Lake and Porter counties in Northwest Indiana and much of northern Illinois. It says several waves of rain, and possibly a few thunderstorms, are likely through Thursday night, with 1 to 3 inches of rain on a widespread basis, and that repeated rounds of rain over saturated soils may flood low-lying and poor drainage areas and raise area rivers. The outlook means higher water is possible but not yet certain, and flood watches, warnings, or advisories could follow. For La Porte County, the Weather Prediction Center (part of the National Weather Service) has a Marginal Risk of flooding rain today (at least a 5% chance) and a Slight Risk from Thursday morning into Friday morning (at least a 15% chance). Today is a good day to clear leaves from gutters and storm drains. If you come to a flooded road, turn around: NWS notes that 12 inches of rushing water can carry away most cars. The Storm Prediction Center has no severe storm risk for La Porte today through Friday; on Thursday, La Porte is in its general thunderstorm area, meaning storms are possible but not expected to be severe. Today's severe risk areas are over the southern Plains and parts of Kansas and southern Nebraska.

corrections.text: NWS writes La Porte's forecast times in Eastern time, and we copied two of them without switching to our Central time. Thursday's showers are likely before 4 p.m. (not 5 p.m.), and Friday's before 1 p.m. (not 2 p.m.). The rest of the forecast is unchanged.

posts.title: Foggy start, then sunny and 75 — rain likely Thursday afternoon and night
posts.summary: Patchy fog this morning, then sunny with a high near 75; a 30% chance of showers Wednesday, then showers likely Thursday afternoon (60%) and Thursday night (80%), when a thunderstorm is possible.
body: Today (Tuesday): patchy fog before 9 a.m., then sunny, with a high near 75. The wind is calm this morning and turns south around 5 mph this afternoon. At 5:55 a.m. the La Porte airport reported fog, a half mile of visibility, and 46 degrees, and a Special Weather Statement covers all of La Porte County for fog and locally dense fog this morning. If you're driving early, slow down, leave extra following distance, use your low beams, and watch for children waiting for the school bus. Tonight: mostly cloudy, with a low around 58 and a south wind around 5 mph.

Wednesday: cloudy, high near 73, with a south wind 5 to 10 mph and a 30% chance of showers, mainly between 10 a.m. and 4 p.m. Wednesday night: cloudy and mild, low around 63, with a 20% chance of showers. Thursday: showers likely, mainly after 1 p.m. (60%), with a high near 76 and a southwest wind 5 to 15 mph. Thursday night: showers and possibly a thunderstorm (80%), low around 57. NWS says a tenth to a quarter of an inch of rain is possible Thursday, and a half to three quarters of an inch Thursday night. If you have outdoor work or projects, today is the dry day to get them done.

What changed since yesterday's Scoop: Wednesday is no longer dry; it now has a 30% chance of showers, and its high fell to 73 (from 77). Wednesday night's 20% chance now covers the whole night, not just after 1 a.m. Thursday's rain shifted later: the daytime chance fell to 60% (from 80%) and no longer mentions a thunderstorm, while Thursday night rose to 80% (from 60%), with showers and possibly a thunderstorm. Thursday's high rose to 76 (from 74), and Friday's chance rose to 50% (from 30%). Today and tonight each came in warmer (75 and 58, from 74 and 56). Yesterday, NWS Northern Indiana forecasters said thunderstorms were possible Thursday but severe weather and heavy rain were not expected, with low confidence beyond Thursday. Today they expect rain late Thursday into early Friday, around an inch for most locations, but still no severe weather or significant flooding, with the best thunderstorm chance later Thursday and Thursday night. They add that spotty showers could creep into areas north of US-6 on Wednesday while most of the area stays dry, and that trends point to a dry, cooler weekend that looks to continue into next week.

Right now, a Special Weather Statement for fog and locally dense fog covers all of La Porte County this morning, north and south, including La Porte and Michigan City. There are no watches, warnings, or advisories. The Storm Prediction Center has no severe storm risk for La Porte today through Thursday; its risk areas are over southern and eastern New Mexico and west Texas today, the southern Plains into Kansas and far southern Nebraska on Wednesday, and the southern Plains on Thursday, all far from La Porte. SPC does include La Porte in its general thunderstorm area for Thursday, meaning storms are possible but not expected to be severe.

posts.title: Foggy start, then dry and warmer through Wednesday — rain likely Thursday
posts.summary: A foggy start, with a Dense Fog Advisory for southern La Porte County until 9 a.m., then gradual clearing and a high near 71; dry and warmer through Wednesday, with rain likely Thursday (80%).
body: Today (Monday): a Dense Fog Advisory is in effect until 9 a.m. for southern La Porte County, where visibility may drop to a quarter mile or less, and a Special Weather Statement covers the whole county, including La Porte and Michigan City, for fog and locally dense fog this morning. At 6:15 a.m. the La Porte airport reported fog, a quarter mile of visibility, and 46 degrees, so if you're driving early, slow down, leave extra following distance, and use your low beams. Areas of fog linger until about 10 a.m.; after that, it's mostly cloudy, then gradually sunny, with a high near 71 and a light north wind around 5 mph this afternoon. Tonight: partly cloudy, low around 50.

Tuesday: mostly sunny, high near 74, with a calm morning and a south wind around 5 mph in the afternoon. Tuesday night: mostly cloudy, low around 56. Wednesday: partly sunny and warmer, high near 77, with a south wind 5 to 10 mph. Wednesday night: mostly cloudy and mild, low around 64, with a 20% chance of showers after 1 a.m. If you have outdoor work or projects, Tuesday and Wednesday are the dry days to get them done.

What changed since yesterday's Scoop: Wednesday went from a 40% chance of showers and thunderstorms to a dry, partly sunny day, and its high rose to 77 (from 72). Wednesday night's chance fell to 20%, and only after 1 a.m. (from 50%), and Tuesday night's 20% chance of showers is gone. Today, tonight, and Tuesday each came in a degree warmer (71, 50, and 74). Thursday is now the one clearly wet day: showers are likely, with an 80% chance (up from 70%), a possible thunderstorm after 1 p.m., and a high near 74 (from 70). Thursday night rose to 60% (from 50%), while Friday eased to 30%, before 1 p.m. (from 40%). Yesterday, NWS Northern Indiana forecasters said the air looked too stable for much thunder and pointed to later Friday through Sunday for any heavy rain. Today they say thunderstorms are possible Thursday but severe weather and heavy rain are not expected, and while their confidence beyond Thursday is low, the forecast trends cooler and drier after that.

Right now, a Dense Fog Advisory covers southern La Porte County until 9 a.m., and a Special Weather Statement for fog and locally dense fog covers the whole county this morning. There are no watches or warnings. The Storm Prediction Center has no severe storm risk for La Porte today through Wednesday; it isn't forecasting severe storms anywhere in the country today or Tuesday, and its Wednesday risk area is over the Plains, far from La Porte.

posts.title: Dry through Tuesday — then on-and-off rain, with Thursday the wettest day
posts.summary: Patchy fog early, then sunny with a high near 69; dry through Tuesday, then showers return midweek, with the best chance (70%) on Thursday.
body: Today (Sunday): patchy fog before 7 a.m., then sunny, with a high near 69. The wind stays calm this morning and turns north around 5 mph this afternoon. It's a cool start, 45 degrees at the La Porte airport at 5:35 a.m., so if you're driving early, watch for fog in low spots. Tonight: partly cloudy and not as chilly, with a low around 51.

Monday: mostly sunny, high near 70. Monday night: mostly clear, low around 49. Tuesday: sunny and a little warmer, high near 73. Clouds move in Tuesday night, with a 20% chance of showers after 1 a.m. If you have outdoor work or projects, Monday and Tuesday are the dry days to get them done.

What changed since yesterday's Scoop: Wednesday dropped to a 40% chance of showers and thunderstorms (from about 50%) and Wednesday night to 50% (from about 60%), while Thursday is now the wettest day, with showers likely and a 70% chance (up from about 60%). Showers stay possible Friday (40%) and next Saturday. Yesterday, NWS Northern Indiana forecasters named Saturday as their early pick for any stronger storms. Today they say the air looks too stable for much thunder through the late workweek, so this looks more like on-and-off rain than a stormy stretch. Their best chance for heavy rain is later Friday through Sunday, and only if a stalled front sets up just right. They expect the rain to clear out by early next week.

Right now there are no watches, warnings, or advisories for La Porte County. The Storm Prediction Center has no severe storm risk for La Porte today through Tuesday; in fact, it isn't forecasting severe storms anywhere in the country on Monday or Tuesday.

posts.title: Sunny and dry through Tuesday — rain chances return midweek and may linger
posts.summary: Sunny today with a high near 69 and a chilly night; dry through Tuesday, then showers and storms become possible Wednesday into next weekend.
body: Today (Saturday): sunny, with a high near 69 and a light east wind around 5 mph. Tonight: mostly clear and chilly, with a low around 45. If you're camping or out early Sunday, bring a warm layer.
Sunday: mostly sunny, high near 68. Sunday night: partly cloudy, low around 49. Monday: sunny, high near 71. The dry stretch holds through Tuesday, with a high near 73.

What changed since yesterday's Scoop: NWS has slowed the midweek rain and spread it out. Wednesday is now about a 50% chance of showers and thunderstorms (yesterday it was about 60%), and the best odds, near 60%, have moved to Wednesday night and Thursday. Showers stay in the forecast for Friday. NWS Northern Indiana forecasters say a front could stall over the area and keep showers going into next weekend, and that it's still uncertain how much heavy rain or thunder we'll get. If any day brings stronger storms, their early pick is next Saturday. That's a week out, so expect changes.

Right now there are no watches, warnings, or advisories for La Porte County, and the Storm Prediction Center has no thunderstorm risk outlined for La Porte today through Monday. The Flood Warning we mentioned yesterday for the St. Marys River near Decatur is no longer in effect.

posts.title: A dry, crisp weekend — next storm chance arrives Wednesday
posts.summary: Sunny, cool weekend with highs near 69; a cold front brings showers and storms midweek.
body: Quiet weather rules the weekend in La Porte. High pressure keeps skies mostly sunny with no rain in the forecast. Expect lows in the upper 40s tonight and Saturday night, highs near 69 on Saturday and Sunday, and low 70s on Monday and Tuesday.

The next change arrives midweek. A cold front brings a chance of showers late Tuesday night, then showers and thunderstorms are likely on Wednesday, with about a 60% chance of rain. NWS Northern Indiana forecasters say an isolated strong storm is possible, depending on when the front arrives. If you're traveling or camping Wednesday, that's the day to keep an eye on.
Right now there are no watches, warnings, or advisories for La Porte County, and the Storm Prediction Center has no thunderstorm risk outlined for our area through Sunday.

Travel note: this is great camping weather, but mornings in the 40s call for a warm layer. If you're headed to northeast Indiana, NWS has a Flood Warning out for the St. Marys River near Decatur (Adams and Allen counties) through Saturday evening.

posts.title: Week ahead: dry and mild start, then a wetter, unsettled second half
posts.summary: Dry through Tuesday with highs in the low 70s; showers and storms become possible Wednesday and may linger into next weekend.
body: Early week (Mon–Tue): quiet. NWS expects sunshine and dry weather in La Porte through Tuesday, with highs near 71 on Monday and 73 on Tuesday and cool nights in the upper 40s. It's a good window for outdoor work and travel.

Midweek (Wed–Thu): rain chances return. Showers and thunderstorms become possible late Tuesday night, with about a 50% chance on Wednesday and the best odds, near 60%, Wednesday night and Thursday. NWS Northern Indiana forecasters say it's still uncertain how much heavy rain or thunder we'll get. If you're traveling or camping midweek, plan around Wednesday night and Thursday.

Late week into next weekend: showers may hang around. Forecasters say a front could stall over the area from Thursday into the weekend and keep showers going (Friday is about a 45% chance). If any day brings stronger thunderstorms, their early pick is Saturday, Oct. 3, which is still a week out.

Across the Midwest: NOAA's Climate Prediction Center, in its outlook for Oct. 1–5, favors warmer-than-normal temperatures for most of the eastern U.S. and leans wetter than normal for most of the country east of the Rockies, especially the Southern Plains and the Lower Mississippi, Tennessee, and Ohio Valleys. For Oct. 3–9, it favors near-normal temperatures from the Southern Plains northeast into the Great Lakes, and wetter than normal for the central and eastern U.S.

What it means for you: enjoy the quiet start, plan an indoor backup for Wednesday night and Thursday, and run your route through the Trip Planner before any travel late in the week. These outlooks are probabilities, not guarantees, so check back as the week unfolds.
